newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: U.S. eyes lucrative Asia defence market.
newsitem.headline: U.S. eyes lucrative Asia defence market.

text.p: U.S. companies will take part in Singapore's Asia Defence trade show next month as they try to step up their presence in the rapidly growing regional arms market, a United States official said on Wednesday.
Top defence officials from up to 13 countries including China, Japan and India will take part in a parallel January 15-17 conference, organisers told a news briefing.
"I don't think they would come here if they do not see a commercial advantage," U.S. embassy spokesman Michael Anderson said when asked about the presence of U.S. companies.
"I would think that's a major reason why any private sector company would come over," he said.
One of the U.S. firms taking part in the defence trade show will be McDonnell Douglas, whose proposed $13 billion merger with Boeing was announced this week.
"I believe the (arms) market is growing fairly rapidly and is one of the fastest growing in the world," said Edward Liu of the Singapore Institute of International Affairs.

Many Southeast Asian countries have beefed up their arsenals over the past few years. Singapore, Indonesia and Thailand bought U.S.-made F-16 fighter-bombers while Malaysia has MIG-29 planes in its air force.
Liu said the conference would also discuss the strategic situation in the region.
Philippine Security Minister Jose Almonte and retired U.S. Admiral William Owens, a former deputy chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff, are scheduled to speak at the conference.
The defence ministers of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) were also invited to the meeting, although the organisers could not say who would attend.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
